bandReport.notes: 25 questions, Q41-Q65 contiguous, no gaps and no duplicates. Printed page numbers are 13-A (p06), 15-A (p07), 17-A (p08), 19-A (p09) — the booklet's even printed pages are blank/not rendered, so the four PNGs are consecutive question-bearing pages and nothing sits between them. Q41 (p06 left column top) starts fresh — stem, all four options complete, nothing continues from p05. Q47 (p06 right column) ends at option (d) 'Nehruvian Socialism' at the foot of the column and is complete; p07 opens cleanly at Q48. Q54 (p07 right column) ends at option (d) 'Satyavadu Parinaya', complete. Q60 (p08 right column) ends at option (d), complete. Q65 (p09 right column) ends at option (d) 'Neither 1 nor 2', complete — nothing spills to p10, which belongs to B3 and should open at Q66. No shared/Directions code block anywhere in this band; every question carries its own four printed options. No figures, graphs or diagrams in this band. Every option block sits directly beneath its own stem in the same column — no cross-column option runs. All code-option rows (Q46, Q50, Q55, Q62, Q63, Q65) were re-read from 7-9x crops of the source PDF rather than inferred: Q55's four code rows are (a) 2 1 4 3, (b) 2 4 1 3, (c) 3 4 1 2, (d) 3 1 4 2; Q50's option order is the unusual '1, 2 and 3' / '2 and 3 only' / '2 only' / '1 and 3 only'; Q63's is '1 and 2 only' / '1, 2, 3 and 4' / '4 only' / '1, 2 and 4 only'. Q42 option (a) genuinely prints '175 days' (verified at 9x) — a deliberate distractor against the Act's real 100 days, not a transcription slip. Q57 and Q58 print their options with terminal full stops; transcribed as printed. No catalog gaps: every question mapped to an existing chapter. Two classifications worth a second eye at merge — Q48 (BRICS, 'which best describes') filed as Polity > World Polity > United Nations and Global Institutions because it tests what the grouping IS, not a dated summit event; Q53 (Hampi ruins brought to light by an East India Company officer) filed under Medieval India > Vijayanagara Empire since Hampi is the Vijayanagara capital, though the question is really colonial antiquarianism and the catalog has no subtopic for that.
